To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the interface region of a bi-layer tablet experiences an elastic relaxation during the tablet ejection stage of compaction process and that this relaxation is influenced by the interface bonding strength.

the elastic relaxation in a bi-layered tablets during the ejection process is dependent on the interface strength, and the tablet height elastic expansion is influenced by the elastic relaxation that occurs at the interface region.

the elastic relaxation of the tablet during the ejection is influenced by the interfacial bonding, where the increase in interfacial bonding strength reduces the tablet elastic relaxation during ejection.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interfacial mechanical properties of the bi-layered tablets during the ejection process.
the understanding of the interfacially elastic relaxation of bi-layered tablet during the ejection phase of the compaction cycle.
the elastic deformation of bi-layered tablet during the ejection process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the elastic relaxation in a bi-layered tablets interface region is governed by a combination of the plastic and elastic bonding.
the interface strength affects both the elastic relaxation of the tablet during ejection, and the tablet elastic recovery during the relaxation period after ejection.
the increase in the tablet interface bonding strength reduces the occurrence of the tablet elastic relaxation in the ejection stage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the interface strength is an important factor to consider in the design of the bi-layered tablets for controlled release solid dosage forms.
the increase in the interfacial bonding between the two layers in a bi-layered system would result in the improvement of the overall tablet integrity.
the increase in the interfacial strength would lead to a reduction in the elastic relaxation in both the interfacial and tablet height regions during ejection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the elastic relaxation of the bi-layered tablets is governed by the interface region properties.
the elastic relaxation during the tablet ejection process is the governing factor that determines the tablet interface strength.
the elastic relaxation in both diametrical and axial directions during the ejection is governed by the interfacial bonding strength and plastic deformation.
